body.note:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Scales. Brand-independent.

   A brand pack may override any of these, but most packs will not — a brand
   changes what things look like, rarely how they are proportioned. Colour and
   anything else a brand genuinely owns lives in the pack, not here.

   Everything is rem. No vw in the type scale: fluid type built on viewport
   units does not respond to the user's browser font-size setting, which is
   what WCAG 1.4.4 actually tests at 200%. Container-relative sizing, where a
   component wants it, is expressed per-component with cqi.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

items.note:
--- space: a 4px base with a doubling tail -------------------------
       The private ramp. The public --tk-space-* tokens are this times
       --tk-density, derived just below.
       ------------------------------------------------------------------

Manrope is the kit's own face — see src/css/fonts/manrope.css for
       what it is and why it is here. "Manrope Fallback" is a metric-matched
       stand-in so the swap costs no layout shift; the generic stack after it
       is what runs if neither loads. A brand pack overrides this slot like
       any other.

items.note:
Display face and case. Default to the body face and no transform, so
       the kit reads as one voice until a pack says otherwise.

Lucide's own default. A pack with a heavy display face usually wants
       more than this; a quiet one usually wants less.

Icon box, in rem, so a reader at 200% gets icons at 200% along with the
       text beside them. These were three numbers in Icon.tsx — 16, 20, 24 —
       which meant icon size was the one measurement in the kit that ignored
       the root size, ignored a pack, and could only be changed by editing
       TypeScript.

--- leading and tracking ---------------------------------------------
       Type does not scale linearly and neither should its spacing. The same
       tracking from caption to display is the single loudest tell that a
       scale was listed rather than designed: at 12px a face needs air, at
       48px the same air reads as a gap. Leading runs the other way — long
       body lines need it, a two-word headline does not.

       So the ramp is paired. Larger step, tighter leading, tighter tracking.
       --tk-*-display is the top of the ramp; the older four leading values
       and three tracking values keep their names and meanings.
       --------------------------------------------------------------------
Surface seed: large enough that pad (space-4/5) leaves a visible inner curve.

Concentric nesting. A rounded box inside a rounded box has one correct
       inner radius: the outer radius less the gap between them. Any other
       value leaves two arcs that do not share a centre, which is what makes a
       card with an inset plate look approximate no matter how careful the
       rest of it is. Clamped at zero, because past that the inner corner is
       square and square is correct.

       Surfaces that bleed to their parent's edge do not use this — they
       inherit the parent's radius exactly. See card-media.

--tk-radius-nested is NOT a value, it is a running total. See the
       concentric-radius block at the foot of this file.

--- plate ------------------------------------------------------------
       The cap is the point. A plate is the one element whose height comes from
       its ratio rather than its content, so in a fluid grid it is what makes
       the page lurch — measured at +1785px in one step when the insights feed
       dropped from four columns to one. It keeps its ratio until it reaches
       this, then stops.
       --------------------------------------------------------------------

--- scrim ------------------------------------------------------------
       Derived in src/css/components/scrim.css, not chosen. Each alpha is the
       lightest wash that still guarantees its contrast ratio when the image
       underneath is pure white — the worst case an unknown photograph can
       present. The gate composites them and checks the arithmetic.
       --------------------------------------------------------------------

How far up the gradient holds full alpha. Text must sit inside this
       band or the guarantee above does not apply to it.
How far from the anchor edge the wash reaches. 100% = full frame.

The manual-level escape hatch and its bounds. 0.25 is the point below
       which a wash stops reading as a wash; 0.88 is the point above which
       there is no photograph left. Neither is a compliance threshold — those
       are the three above.
Frost radius over the same conceptual range.

The per-instance overrides. Declared here so the lint can see them and
       so every one has a documented default rather than appearing out of a
       style attribute.

--- measure ----------------------------------------------------------
       Set from tools/type-gate.mjs, not by eye. `ch` is the advance width of
       the digit zero, which is wider than the average character, so a measure
       in `ch` always renders MORE characters per line than its number
       suggests — 68ch measured at 80 CPL, well past the comfortable band.
       56ch lands at ~66, which is the middle of the 45-75 range.
       -------------------------------------------------------------------

items.$comment: measured: 66.7 CPL in Manrope (the type gate's body row)

items.note:
--- motion -----------------------------------------------------------
       The raw material: four durations and three curves. A component never
       names these directly, for the same reason it never names a hex — they
       are the ramp, not the contract.
       --------------------------------------------------------------------

For loops that run for seconds, not transitions: a sweep, an orbit, an
       ambient drift. Always linear, always stopped under reduced motion.

Loops that say "still working": a spinner turning, a skeleton breathing.
       Short and steady, and stopped under reduced motion like the rest.

--- motion contract ---------------------------------------------------
       One motion token per kind of change, each a complete `<duration> <easing>`
       so a component writes

           transition: background-color var(--tk-motion-surface);

       and never picks a number. Pairing motion to WHAT MOVES rather than to a
       t-shirt size is what makes it consistent: every surface in the kit
       changes at the same rate because they all read the same slot, and a
       brand that wants to feel quicker moves one value rather than auditing
       every component for stray 200ms.

       These are pack slots. Pace and curve are as much a brand's property as
       its greys — the packs below fill them, and packs/_template.css lists
       them with the rest.

       Ordered by how much of the screen each one disturbs: ink and surface
       are instant-feeling, size and position are the slowest, because a box
       changing shape is the one the eye actually has to follow.
       --------------------------------------------------------------------

--- elevation: expressed as line + shadow so a flat wireframe pack
           can zero the shadow and keep the boundary ---------------------

An overlay above the page (a dialog), and the lift a card-like control
       takes on hover. Every pack flattens sm, md and lg (a dialog stands off
       its scrim by its border), and keeps the lift. The dialog used to write
       its own "var(--tk-shadow-md), 0 24px 48px …", which is invalid once md
       is none, so no pack ever drew it: lg is that shadow, said once.

--- density: the single knob context turns.
           Components multiply their own padding by it. -------------------

body.note:
Density is contextual, not owned. Any ancestor can set it and every
     component below resolves against it.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Density.

   Density used to be applied at the call site — `calc(var(--tk-space-5) *
   var(--tk-density))`, written out in each component that remembered to. Six
   files did. The shells did not, so `data-gap` ignored density entirely, and
   neither did any section padding, so the whole compact/comfortable range moved
   a page by about twelve pixels. A multiplier you have to remember is a
   multiplier that is mostly absent.

   So the scale carries it instead: --tk-space-* IS the ramp times the density
   in force, and every consumer gets it for free — shells, components, and the
   inline styles in the audit rebuilds alike. No call site multiplies any more.

   Why the derivation is repeated on [data-density] rather than written once on
   :root: a custom property is substituted at computed-value time and then
   INHERITED AS A VALUE. Declared only on :root, --tk-space-5 would compute
   against :root's density and descendants would inherit that number — the same
   trap that makes a pack re-declare `color` instead of trusting the token to
   re-resolve. Restating it on every element that can change --tk-density is
   what makes a nested density region actually nest.

   --tk-target-min is deliberately NOT in the ramp. Pointer targets have a
   floor in WCAG 2.5.8 and density is not allowed to argue with it.

   [data-brand] is in the selector for the same reason [data-density] is, and
   it was missing until a pack tried to set its own density. A brand that owns
   proportion sets --tk-density in its pack; without restating the ramp on
   [data-brand] that pack inherits the space tokens ROOT already computed and
   the density silently does nothing — the page looks identical and nothing
   reports a problem, which is the worst kind of bug this file can have. The
   same applies to --tk-radius-nested below: a pack that changes --tk-radius-xl
   has to re-seed the concentric chain or every nested corner on its pages
   keeps solving from the kit's radius instead of the brand's.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

items.note:
The seed for the concentric chain below: a container with nothing
       around it rounds at --tk-radius-xl (was lg; lg is now a mid step). Re-stated here because the space
       ramp changes with density and so does every subtraction downstream.

Control shapes: the corner a brand gives its inputs and its buttons.
       Shapes, like capsules, not steps in the concentric chain: a control
       takes its brand's corner wherever it sits, capped by the nested radius
       so it is never rounder than what holds it. Inputs default to md, which
       is a rounded rectangle in every pack; before this they took the nested
       radius, which at page level is xl, and on a 40px control that is a
       capsule in every pack with an xl over 20px. Buttons keep the nested
       radius (the 9999px initial value loses every min()); a pack that wants
       its buttons to match its inputs sets --tk-radius-button. Restated on
       [data-brand] so a pack's own md is the one that resolves.

Display sizes that give way on a phone. Measured before they existed
       (the ds-corpus type brief said: measure first): at 412px, nine of the
       kit's page and hero titles ran to four lines at their desktop sizes.
       So the three top styles are fluid between the step below and their
       own step: the step below at a 360px viewport, rising until their own
       at 960px, fixed above. The bounds are the pack's own sizes (restated
       on [data-brand], so a brand's 4xl is the one that resolves); only the
       slope is the kit's, and it is set by the widest step any pack has
       (door-shop's 3xl to 4xl is 28px), so every pack reaches its own size
       by 960px: display covers a 30px step, title 18px, heading 12px. CSS
       cannot divide a width by a width yet, or the slope would be the
       pack's. Every onion skin is taken at 1000px or wider, so the design
       file's fixed sizes are still exact there.

The page gutter: the one space between the screen's edge and the
       content, applied once (the center shell, and any band that meets the
       edge) and never by a band AND the content inside it. Space-4 on a
       phone and up to 80rem; space-5 from 80rem (see below), Primer's numbers. The
       ds-corpus spacing brief; Primer's content padding. Before this, the
       center shell padded 16px and the bands 24px, and PageHero's band
       padded around a center shell, so a title lost both.

Control heights: a button or an icon button, and a field. Scaled by
       density, never below the pointer-target floor. They were the same
       formula written out in button.css and twice in modal.css (the room
       its header keeps for Close), and once in field.css. Figma has them as
       control/min and field/min, per density mode.

body.note:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Concentric radii.

   One rule, everywhere: **the inner radius is the outer radius less the gap
   between them.** Two rounded boxes whose arcs do not share a centre look
   approximate no matter how careful the rest of the page is, and the eye
   catches it long before anyone can say why. A system that picks radius-sm for
   inner things and radius-lg for outer things is guessing at that centre
   rather than computing it.

   A single global "nested radius" token cannot express this, which is what the
   kit had and what was wrong with it: the correct inner radius depends on
   which container you are in and how much padding that container has. A card
   inset by space-5 and an alert inset by space-4 do not want the same number.

   So --tk-radius-nested is a running total. Every rounded container does this:

     :where([data-tk="thing"]) {
       --_radius: var(--tk-radius-nested);      what I was handed
       --_radius-gap: var(--tk-space-5);        what I inset my children by
       border-radius: var(--_radius);
     }
     :where([data-tk="thing"]) > * {
       --tk-radius-nested: max(0px, calc(var(--_radius) - var(--_radius-gap)));
     }

   The subtraction is published on the CHILDREN, not on the container, and that
   is not a style choice — it is the only arrangement that works. A custom
   property reference resolves against the element's OWN computed value, so a
   container that both reads --tk-radius-nested and re-declares it is a cycle:
   both properties become guaranteed-invalid, border-radius falls back to its
   initial value, and every rounded box on the page silently squares off. That
   is exactly what the first version of this did. Declaring on `> *` reads the
   inherited value on one element and writes on another, so there is no cycle.

   Three things are deliberately outside the chain:

   - Capsules. --tk-radius-full is a shape, not a rounded rectangle. A pill
     inside a card stays a pill; subtracting a gap from it is meaningless.
   - Bleeding surfaces. A child flush to its parent's edge has no gap to
     subtract, so it takes the parent's corners exactly and the parent clips.
   - Square things. Zero stays zero; max() already guarantees it.

   tools/radius-gate.mjs walks every built story and checks the arithmetic.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
